title: FAUST - VIII. The protostellar disc of VLA 1623-2417W and its streamers imaged by ALMA
question: Investigate the gas in the disk of VLA 1623W and its dynamical interaction with the other protostellar sources in the VLA 1623 multiple protostellar system using ALMA 1.3 mm continuum and C18O (2-1) observations.

data.sensitivity: 1.8 mJy beam^-1 per channel for C18O 12-m datacube; 1.4 mJy beam^-1 per channel for C18O 12-m+7-m datacube; 0.26 mJy beam^-1 for continuum map

what.value: Distance to Ophiuchus A / VLA 1623 of d = 131 pc

evidence.quote: VLA1623 is located in Ophiuchus A at a distance, $d$, of 131 pc (cite: Gagne2018),

what.value: Dust opacity at 1.3 mm of 2.17 cm^2 g^-1

evidence.quote: We assume isothermal conditions and optically thin emission, dust opacity ($\kappa_{\nu}$) at 1.3 mm of 2.17 cm$^{2}$g$^{-1}$ (Zamponi et al. submitted),

what.value: CS(5-4) emission map probing outflow cavity walls and systemic velocity of VLA 1623AB (+3.8 km/s)

evidence.quote: The magenta contour indicates the $25\sigma$ level of the CS(5–4) emission integrated on the velocity interval 3.4 – 4.2 km s$^{-1}$, which probes the outflow cavity walls associated with VLA 1623A (cite: Ohashi2022).

evidence.loc: Hypothesis 1: formation in a separate core
evidence.quote: while our observations indicate that VLA 1623W has a systemic velocity of $+1.6$ km s$^{-1}$, which differs from the systemic velocity of VLA 1623AB ($+3.8$ km s$^{-1}$) and the two ridges.

what.value: VLA X-band (3.6 cm) continuum positions from 1991.8 (project AB817)

evidence.quote: combining our FAUST ALMA Band 6 observations of the continuum at 1.3 mm, taken in 2019, with the data at 3.6 cm, taken with the VLA in the X-band in 1991 ((cite: Andre1993), project AB817).

recipe.goal: Fit 1.3 mm continuum emission to measure source positions, sizes, PAs, and fluxes
recipe.method: Two-dimensional elliptical Gaussian fitting on the 12-m + 7-m 1.3 mm continuum image
assumptions: Elliptical Gaussian morphology for disk continuum; disk inclination derived from fitted aspect ratio (i ~ 80 deg for W)

recipe.goal: Estimate disk dust and total masses from 1.3 mm continuum flux
recipe.method: Analytic optically thin isothermal dust mass calculation from integrated 1.3 mm continuum flux: M_dust = (F_1.3mm * d^2) / (kappa_nu * B_nu(T_dust))
assumptions: Isothermal conditions and optically thin dust emission
Dust opacity at 1.3 mm kappa_nu = 2.17 cm^2 g^-1
Dust temperature T_dust between 20 K and 50 K

recipe.goal: Map spatial distribution and kinematics of C18O (2-1) emission in disk and streamers
recipe.method: Generate channel maps, moment 0, and moment 1 maps for low velocities (+0.2 to +3.0 km/s using 12-m + 7-m data) and high velocities (-2.6 to +5.8 km/s using 12-m only data)
key_parameters: Low velocity range: +0.2 to +3.0 km/s; High velocity range: -2.6 to -0.4 km/s and +3.6 to +5.8 km/s (overall -2.6 to +5.8 km/s)

recipe.goal: Estimate dynamical mass of VLA 1623W from high-velocity C18O disk kinematics
recipe.method: Measure radial peak distances of symmetric high-velocity C18O channels and apply Keplerian rotation formula M_dyn = r * V^2 / G
key_parameters: Channels at radial velocities of +/- 2.8 and +/- 3.0 km/s with respect to V_sys = +1.6 km/s, peaking at 0.37'' and 0.33''
assumptions: Keplerian rotation, disk inclination of 80 deg, systemic velocity V_sys(W) = +1.6 km/s, distance d = 131 pc

recipe.goal: Estimate relative proper motions between VLA 1623W and VLA 1623A/B
recipe.method: Compare angular offsets and separations between source W and sources A and B across a 27.7-year baseline using 1991.8 VLA X-band (3.6 cm) and 2019.5 ALMA Band 6 (1.3 mm) continuum positions
key_parameters: Time baseline of 27.7 years between 1991.8 and 2019.5

evidence.quote: We estimate the dynamical mass of VLA 1623W, $M_{\rm dyn}=0.45\pm0.08$ M$_{\rm \ensuremath{\odot}}$, and the mass of its disk, $M_{\rm disk}\sim6\times10^{-3}$ M$_{\rm \ensuremath{\odot}}$.

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: The estimated dynamical mass is $0.45 \pm 0.08$ M$_{\odot}$.
For source W, assuming a gas-to-dust ratio of 100, we obtain a total disk mass of $6\pm3 \times 10^{-3}$ M$_{\odot}$.

score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project code, CASA versions, weighting schemes, beam sizes, noise levels, and exact analytical equations and parameters used to derive disk masses and dynamical masses. However, low-level imaging and self-calibration parameters (scales, thresholds, solints) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Large Program data (2018.1.01205.L) with straightforward, well-specified analysis steps (2D Gaussian fitting with CASA imfit, analytical dust mass equation, and two-channel Keplerian dynamical mass calculation) yielding clear numeric benchmarks.
